public_rationale: No decisive event found meets the early-resolution rule. Continuing hallucinations are consistent with the forecast, but do not prove inevitability. Formal lower bounds depend on specified assumptions, and improvements do not establish elimination. With no stated deadline, the forecast remains open.
limitations: A mathematical reading and a practical-risk reading could yield different assessments.
Company-reported improvements are not independent guarantees.
The search is not an exhaustive inventory of every system or theorem.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Hallucinations in large language models will remain inevitable.

statement.excerpt: And no matter what investors and CEOs might tell you, hallucinations will remain inevitable.

from_speaker: no matter what investors and CEOs might tell you
our_interpretation: The ordinary reading is that useful, general-purpose LLMs will retain some risk of producing false or unsupported assertions.
Inevitable does not mean every answer hallucinates or that error rates cannot fall.
A system that always abstains or operates only in a narrowly verified domain does not by itself settle the general-purpose claim.
Near-zero benchmark error is relevant progress but is not equivalent to demonstrated elimination.
criteria.support_condition: A validated impossibility result establishes unavoidable hallucination under assumptions that genuinely cover useful general-purpose LLMs and their permitted mitigations.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A useful general-purpose LLM system demonstrates a substantiated, independently checked guarantee against hallucinated assertions across its broad intended scope.
